candidates.bio: BALAM KIEL is a Toronto-based Spanish artist whose music blends reggaeton, Latin pop and hip-hop. He has built a solo catalogue including Capítulo Uno while collaborating with Canadian artists such as Snow and Cole James. His appearances with Snow on Reason to Love and Together are the two BALAM KIEL credits in the Northern Dial library.
Vancouver recording artist, producer and director Bdice makes Canadian hip-hop while also working behind the scenes as an engineer, producer and music-video creator.

Beau Dick was a Kwakwaka'wakw artist, hereditary chief, culture bearer, activist, dancer and musician from British Columbia. Born in Alert Bay, his creative practice connected carving, ceremony, performance, song and storytelling, making him an important figure in contemporary Indigenous art in Canada. Northern Dial carries Beau Dick in recognition of that broader musical and cultural practice.

Bebeboy is a Toronto-based R&B and hip-hop artist, songwriter and producer whose melodic catalogue blends contemporary R&B, pop and rap. Born outside Canada and raised within Toronto's music scene, Bebeboy has built an independent catalogue of emotionally direct songs and collaborations. Northern Dial carries Bebeboy as part of its contemporary Toronto R&B catalogue.

Calgary-born Canadian-American singer-songwriter and guitarist Bella White blends bluegrass, country, folk and contemporary Americana. Raised in Alberta around traditional music, she developed a modern songwriting voice while staying closely connected to the Appalachian and bluegrass sounds that shaped her early playing.

Palestinian-Canadian rapper, singer, songwriter and producer Belly was raised in Ottawa and became known for solo hip-hop releases as well as songwriting collaborations with The Weeknd and other major artists.
Markham, Ontario artist Benstar is a Canadian contemporary-R&B singer, songwriter and producer whose independent catalogue centers on melodic vocals and modern R&B production.
Toronto DJ, producer and curator Big Jacks is a Canadian music figure known for deep R&B and hip-hop knowledge, vinyl culture and co-founding the Toronto-based GGBR Records & Tapes.

Big Lysh is a Toronto hip-hop artist whose independent catalogue includes tracks such as Turks, 5am In Houston and Count That Cash. Her music sits within Toronto's contemporary rap scene, with releases and visuals distributed across major streaming and social platforms. Northern Dial carries Big Lysh as part of its ongoing coverage of emerging Canadian hip-hop.
Toronto hip-hop producer Big Sproxx is a Canadian beatmaker, engineer and Freedom Writers member known for sample-driven production and collaborations across the city's independent rap scene.

Bijaan is a Calgary-born and based MC whose music blends old-school hip-hop foundations with a global perspective shaped by family roots in East Africa and India. He has performed at events including NXNE, Sled Island and JUNO Week, and his work has earned attention as part of a rising generation of Canadian hip-hop. Northern Dial carries Bijaan as part of its Western Canadian rap catalogue.
Toronto producer, DJ and musician Birthday Boy, born Eoin, makes sample-minded production shaped by the city's hip-hop and club scenes.
Toronto rapper and battle-rap pioneer Bishop Brigante, born Nickolas Parra, was a longtime recording artist and key figure in Canada's battle-rap community before his death in 2025.

Black Bear, also known as the Black Bear Singers, is an Atikamekw powwow drum group from Manawan, Quebec. Formed in 2000, the group performs northern contemporary music in Atikamekw and has collaborated extensively with The Halluci Nation, including on R.E.D.

Scarborough rapper and producer Black Cat is a member of the Canadian hip-hop group IRS and the larger Monolith collective. Alongside Korry Deez and producer T.R.A.C.K.S., he helped shape IRS’s Welcome to Planet IRS era and Toronto underground records connected to Monolith and Mastermind.

Black U Sun is a Toronto underground hip-hop artist documented on the 1998 local compilation Invading the Mega City. Black U Sun appears with Alsham and K.P. on 'Mega Garden,' the same recording carried by Northern Dial. The release captures Toronto's independent hip-hop scene of the period.

Black-I was a Toronto hip-hop MC and dancer who emerged from the city's 1990s underground scene. A former backup dancer for Maestro Fresh Wes, he appeared on the landmark Canadian compilation Rap Essentials Volume One and later alongside Maestro and Ghetto Concept. Quintessential from Maestro's Built to Last and Ghetto Concept's Westend Story are his two Northern Dial library credits.
Montréal trio blesse grew out of Zen Bamboo and blends francophone alternative rock with indie, bedroom-pop and hyperpop influences in a collaborative Québec project.

Canadian producer, composer and songwriter Mischa "Book" Chillak is credited as Book on the 2019 single "On the Move" with Toronto artist Rochester. Chillak has also worked in film, television and commercial music and released material under the Mischa 'Book' Chillak name.

Boomtang is the shortened name used by Toronto dance-pop production group The Boomtang Boys for their 2002 album Wet. Built around Rob DeBoer and Tony Grace, the Canadian project followed earlier hits such as Squeeze Toy with Movin' On, which reached number one on the Canadian singles chart.

Boy Wonder is a Toronto musician and independent artist whose work sits within the city's contemporary music scene. He is distinct from similarly named producers and is documented specifically as a musician from Toronto. Northern Dial carries Boy Wonder as part of its Canadian independent artist catalogue.

Halifax MC Boy-Ill, born Matt Boyle, came up in Nova Scotia's hip-hop community as a member of Fax4 with Spesh K, Quake Matthews and Markit. He later partnered with longtime friend Markit in Something Good, developing their two-MC setup into a live-band project that toured beyond Halifax.
Toronto hip-hop crew Brass Tacks, built around Battle Cat and Diamond Eye's, emerged from the city's 1990s underground with progressive production, battle-rap roots and independent vinyl releases.
Scarborough hip-hop group Brassmunk combined underground rap, soul and G-funk influences, becoming an important part of Toronto's late-1990s and 2000s hip-hop scene.

Brigitte M is a Quebec singer and stage performer whose career spans pop, musical theatre and orchestral reinterpretations of rock songs. Known professionally as Brigitte M and born Brigitte Marchand, she has appeared in major Quebec productions including Grease and released solo albums such as Toute moi and From Metal to Crystal. Northern Dial carries Brigitte M as part of its francophone Canadian vocal catalogue.

BriskInTheHouse is a Toronto hip-hop artist working within the city's independent rap scene. His online catalogue identifies Toronto as his location and collects original tracks and collaborations from his ongoing recording work. Northern Dial carries BriskInTheHouse as part of its Toronto hip-hop catalogue.
Québec singer Bruno Pelletier is a major francophone pop and musical-theatre performer whose career includes multiple Félix awards, platinum-selling albums and prominent stage roles.

buddie is a Vancouver-based grunge-pop and indie-rock band led by songwriter Dan Forrest. Originally formed in Philadelphia, the project was rebuilt in Vancouver after Forrest relocated there in 2021, and the current group has become part of the city's independent music scene through releases including Agitator and Glass and appearances at Canadian festivals such as Sled Island and Music Waste.
Toronto-born R&B singer-songwriter Bénita is a Canadian vocalist and Juno-nominated songwriter whose work combines contemporary soul, intimate songwriting and polished pop production.

C4 is a Toronto rapper associated with the Jane and Finch area and the city's underground street-rap scene. He has also been connected with The Corps and appears in Toronto hip-hop coverage under the name C4, including the alias Fourrrr. Northern Dial carries C4 as part of its Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Edmonton-born Rollie Pemberton grew up around hip-hop through his father, pioneering radio DJ Teddy Pemberton, while also absorbing the city's experimental electronic scene. As Cadence Weapon, he brought those worlds together on the 2005 independent version of Breaking Kayfabe and its wider 2006 release, pairing tightly written rap with abrasive, synthetic production at a time when Canadian hip-hop was still often framed through Toronto. The record began a career defined by regional perspective and a willingness to treat electronic music as part of rap's vocabulary rather than a separate scene.

Hope in Dirt City expanded the sound with live instrumentation, and later records continued to shift between club music, experimental production and social observation. Parallel World became the defining statement of that approach. Released in 2021, the album examined Black life, surveillance, displacement, policing and urban inequality through what Pemberton described as a journalistic lens. It won the Polaris Music Prize after earlier Cadence Weapon records had already reached the prize's shortlist. Rollercoaster, released in 2024, turned that critical attention toward platforms, algorithms and the strange economics of online culture.

Pemberton's significance extends beyond recording. He served as Edmonton's poet laureate from 2009 to 2011 and later published the memoir Bedroom Rapper, making writing about place and culture a parallel part of his practice. In Canadian hip-hop, Cadence Weapon is important because he offers a different map of the genre: Edmonton roots, Montréal and Toronto connections, experimental electronic production and sustained criticism of how technology and cities shape everyday life.

CAIRO! is a Hamilton, Ontario artist and producer whose catalogue blends hip-hop, phonk and electronic production. Born Cairo Khaleel Weir, he began making beats in 2016 and has since built an independent catalogue that includes collaborations across the contemporary phonk and underground rap scenes. Northern Dial carries CAIRO! as part of its contemporary Ontario hip-hop catalogue.

Calamine, the stage name of Julie Gagnon, is a Quebec rapper, beatmaker and DJ whose francophone hip-hop pairs feminist, queer and anti-capitalist writing with self-produced beats. Originally from Sainte-Foy in Quebec City and now associated with Montreal’s scene, she was named a Radio-Canada Revelation and won the Prix Félix-Leclerc de la chanson.

Caleb Awiti is a Kenyan-born, Vancouver-based R&B artist whose music blends contemporary soul, pop and melodic hip-hop influences. His independent catalogue includes releases such as SBLTLA, HYPNOTIC and I Can't Change Time, and his work has been featured in Canadian discovery playlists including Touchpoints: Vancouver. Northern Dial carries Caleb Awiti as part of its contemporary West Coast R&B catalogue.

Calibur is the hip-hop stage name used by Ajax vocalist Najja Crest, who emerged from Durham Region's early-2000s music scene after performing with the groups Foot Soldiers and Bush Life. A contemporary Pickering-area profile identifies Najja 'Calibur' Crest as an Ajax artist who had opened for acts including Boot Camp, Jeru and Ghetto Concept. Northern Dial carries Calibur as part of its Durham Region and Canadian hip-hop catalogue.
Edmonton band Calling All Captains is a Canadian punk-rock group that combines post-hardcore grit, pop-punk melody and emotionally direct alternative-rock songwriting.
Toronto singer-songwriter and producer Cam Kahin makes raw, guitar-driven alternative rock that draws on pop-punk, grunge and emotionally direct songwriting.

Camille is Camille Thomas, one half of the Canadian twin-sister pop duo Carmen & Camille. Northern Dial's Camille entry is tied to 'Shine 4U' and 'Shine 4U 2.0,' recordings credited to the duo and their remix collaborators. Carmen & Camille emerged from Vancouver and their single 'Shine 4U' earned a Juno nomination for Dance Recording of the Year.

Capital Vision is a Brampton-rooted Canadian urban music collective and management project founded in 2024. Its releases and artist network connect a group of emerging Peel Region hip-hop acts, including JayTrillz, PHB Hollis, Froboii and Punchinrd. Northern Dial carries Capital Vision as part of its contemporary Brampton and GTA hip-hop catalogue.

Caribou is the principal recording project of Dundas, Ontario-born musician, producer and mathematician Dan Snaith. After beginning his career under the name Manitoba, Snaith developed a catalogue built around constant reinvention, moving through sample-based electronics, psychedelic pop and increasingly dance-oriented production. Under the Caribou name, Andorra became a major breakthrough and won the 2008 Polaris Music Prize, establishing him as one of Canada's most internationally respected electronic artists.

Snaith changed direction again with Swim in 2010, using unstable rhythms, processed vocals and club music as the foundation for songs rather than conventional electronic tracks. Its international reception expanded Caribou's audience substantially, while the more direct and soulful Our Love continued the progression and earned a Grammy nomination. In parallel, Snaith's Daphni project gave him a separate outlet for dance-floor-focused records and DJ culture, allowing the two identities to develop in conversation with each other.

Later Caribou albums Suddenly and Honey continued that pattern of deliberate change, with Honey bringing the pop and communal dance impulses of Caribou and Daphni closer together. Snaith's importance to Canadian music comes from the longevity of that experimentation: he has moved from Ontario's independent electronic underground to major international festival stages without settling into a fixed signature, while retaining a recognizable emphasis on rhythm, melody and meticulous production.

Carmen is Carmen Thomas, one half of the Canadian twin-sister pop duo Carmen & Camille. Northern Dial carries Carmen through 'Shine 4U' and 'Shine 4U 2.0,' recordings tied directly to Carmen & Camille's Juno-nominated Canadian catalogue. The sisters were raised in White Rock, British Columbia and built their early career in Vancouver before expanding internationally.
Hanna, Alberta-born singer, guitarist and songwriter Chad Kroeger is a Canadian rock musician best known as the frontman and primary songwriter of Nickelback.

Chai Sully is a Toronto R&B-pop artist and songwriter whose music blends pop instincts, alternative R&B and an offbeat lyrical sensibility. She has become part of Toronto's emerging independent scene through releases including TRIED IT, LIPS, Princess Peach and Thief (come over); her collaboration DerekFisher with KOTO? and Soft Eyez is the Northern Dial library credit.

Montreal electronic musician, producer and multi-instrumentalist Maxime Morin performs as Champion, also known as DJ Champion, blending programmed beats with live guitar and rock energy. His 2004 debut Chill 'Em All produced the signature track No Heaven and earned major Quebec and Juno recognition.

ChanHays is a Halifax, Nova Scotia producer and DJ whose boom-bap production has connected Atlantic Canada's hip-hop scene with rappers from across North America. His catalogue includes the albums Here and The Creepy as well as the Boldy James collaboration Prisoner of Circumstance, released through Halifax-based Droppin' Science Productions. Get Ahead with Aquakultre and Ghettosocks is his Northern Dial library credit.
Surrey-born Canadian-Punjabi lyricist and songwriter Chani Nattan blends Punjabi musical tradition with contemporary hip-hop and has become a major voice in the global Punjabi music wave.

Winnipeg-born pianist and singer-songwriter Chantal Kreviazuk emerged in the late 1990s with a style built around intimate piano writing, strong melodic instincts and emotionally direct lyrics. Her 1997 debut Under These Rocks and Stones produced songs including "Surrounded" and established her as a major new Canadian adult-alternative voice. A successful cover of "Leaving on a Jet Plane" expanded her soundtrack audience, but the second album Colour Moving and Still became the clearest early statement of her own writing.

Colour Moving and Still went double platinum in Canada and produced "Before You" and "Dear Life." At the 2000 JUNO Awards, Kreviazuk won both Best Female Artist and Best Pop/Adult Album. Later solo records including What If It All Means Something, Ghost Stories and Hard Sail kept her recording career active, but her influence increasingly expanded behind the scenes through songwriting with her husband, Our Lady Peace frontman Raine Maida. Their writing and production work reached major international pop artists as well as film and television projects.

That dual career is the key to Kreviazuk's significance. She is part of the generation that made piano-led singer-songwriter music a substantial Canadian mainstream format in the late 1990s, while her later work helped connect Canadian songwriting talent to the global pop industry. Her and Maida's humanitarian work was also recognized with the JUNO Humanitarian Award in 2014. The result is a career whose importance sits both in the records carrying her own name and in songs written for other voices.

Scarborough producer and MC Charisma, also known as Charisma aka Skizzz, is a member of the Canadian hip-hop collective Monolith. In addition to appearing on Monolith records, he has become a frequent producer for fellow Toronto artists including Dan-e-o and J Shiltz.

Scarborough producer and MC Charisma, also known as Charisma aka Skizzz, is a member of the Canadian hip-hop collective Monolith. In addition to appearing on Monolith records, he has become a frequent producer for fellow Toronto artists including Dan-e-o and J Shiltz.

Toronto rapper and vocalist Charlie Noiir is a Canadian hip-hop artist known for his solo work and as a member of the STAYOUTLATE collective. Earlier in his career he fronted the Toronto duo OSIYM, later developing a melodic, genre-fluid solo catalogue while remaining closely tied to the city's independent rap scene.
